name: granite4-3b-ec-magento
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b (config.json max_position_embeddings 131072). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b: 40 full GQA layers (kv heads 8, head_dim 64) and 0 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-04. A QLoRA finetune of ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b (r=8, alpha=16, 4-bit NF4 via Unsloth, 15.6M trainable of 3,403M) targeting Magento-2 e-commerce structured tasks. ACCEPTED WITH A SHIPPING CAVEAT: the repo root is a 67MB PEFT adapter and the only merged artifact is a Q4_K_M GGUF (2.1GB, q8_0 embeddings); no bf16 merged weights are published. It is therefore not adapter-only in the disqualifying sense - merged weights do exist - and the catalog already carries a 4-bit-only derivative of this same base (granite41-3b-german-tutor-v4-4bit), but no base-vs-4bit ablation is published and the card does not say which artifact the eval ran on. Read the numbers accordingly. Every recorded row is the author's own harness on a SYNTHETIC Magento eval built from the same templates as the training data (475 products disjoint), which the card itself says overstates production quality. Two more limits the card states: only one of the five recorded deltas is a loss (answer generation token-F1 13.2 vs 15.3), and the recipe was transplanted from a different base, so the scores rank bases under a fixed recipe rather than establish an intrinsic ordering. Base rows are zero-shot under the same harness, which is why the base's structured scores look catastrophic - they are dominated by format non-adherence. Licence apache-2.0, repo created 2026-09-04.
